newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S COSTELLO SAYS THAI FUND AIDS STABILITY.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S COSTELLO SAYS THAI FUND AIDS STABILITY.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday that Canberra's US$1 billion financial aid package to Thailand was in Australia's best interests.
"It's not in our interests to see economic instability in our region," Costello told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
The loan is being provided through a currency swap between the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Bank of Thailand.
"It'll be re-purchased from the Reserve Bank at fixed exchange rates so that when the rescue is over there's no exchange rate risk for the Reserve Bank," Costello said.
The aid was aimed at preventing Thailand's currency instability spreading to neighbouring currencies, he said.

"The instability could move from the (Thai) baht into other currencies. These are all important trading partners of Australia and it's important we stabilise their currencies and also that these countries continue growing."
Australia on Monday agreed to join a US$16 billion International Monetary Fund-brokered aid package to help Thailand through a severe financial crisis.
Thailand's economic bubble burst after a prolonged boom which involved over-borrowing from overseas and misallocation of financial resources.
Costello said that if the rescue package succeeded, regional instability would be avoided.
"That's the objective, to stabilise the economic prospects in our immediate trading region," he said.
